prime.problem: You know linear layers need a batch to get busy and attention never does. But a server owner asks one question: how long does a decode step take at this batch and context, and how many tokens per second does that buy? Without one formula that combines the pieces, you can't size a server or say which change will help.
prime.fits: Sixth card, the one the book says to take away from the whole chapter. It combines the KV cache (sampling card), B<sub>crit</sub> (linear layers) and attention's intensity into one step time, which every later card reuses.
expect: the book's Pop Quiz (2.5 ms and 21 ms)
prime.goal: Fill the formula for any model, chip, batch and context; say which term dominates; and predict where throughput flattens and why.

attend: Why does the attention term have no FLOPs side while the MLP term takes a max?
When is the small-batch formula (everything bandwidth-bound) good enough, and when does it undercount?
In the Pop Quiz, what changes between B = 4 and B = 256 that makes the math term win?
Why does throughput flatten toward bandwidth ÷ KV bytes per sequence rather than rising forever?
Why does an H200's extra HBM mostly buy batch rather than per-user speed?

must: Every decode step reads each sequence's KV cache (never compute-bound, never shared) and either reads all weights once or does 2 FLOPs per parameter per token, whichever is longer → T<sub>step</sub> = B·S<sub>KV</sub>/W + max(2·B·N/C, S<sub>params</sub>/W)

Small B → the weight read dominates and is shared → throughput B/T<sub>step</sub> climbs almost linearly; large B → the KV term grows with B while the weight read stays fixed → throughput flattens toward W/S<sub>KV</sub> → per-user speed keeps falling
The max flips to math only past B<sub>crit</sub> → on one H100 with Llama-3.1-8B, HBM fills first (238 sequences at 2k, 59 at 8k) → this model never reaches its compute roofline in decode on one chip

Each term maps to a knob (batch, context × KV size, weight precision, chip count) → the dominant term tells you which knob matters → at 8k and full batch the KV read is 80% of the step, so a smaller KV beats FP8 weights
elevated: Past Bcrit both the KV and math terms grow linearly in B → B/Tstep becomes constant, 1/(SKV/W + 2N/C) → that is the plateau the book's PaLM frontier shows around batch 240
The formula assumes perfect overlap of HBM reads and FLOPs → real XLA and GPU engines overlap imperfectly and add launch and prefill work → treat it as a floor on latency, ceiling on throughput
reference: the Pop Quiz's per-chip plateau (767 tok/s)
the perf-1 cross-check at ~1,100 context (26.26 ms vs 23.86 ms)

compress.prompt: Write the general formula from memory with each term labelled by what is physically read or computed. Under it, draw the Pareto curve (per-user speed vs total throughput) and annotate the steep part, the flat part and the HBM wall with the term that causes each.
checklist: KV term: B × KV bytes per sequence ÷ bandwidth, always memory-bound
MLP term: max of math (2·B·N/C) and weight read (bytes/W)
throughput = B / T<sub>step</sub>; per-user speed = 1 / T<sub>step</sub>
steep part: sharing the weight read; flat part: KV read per sequence; wall: HBM capacity
it's a lower bound on step time

retrieve.q: Explain why doubling the batch past B<sub>crit</sub> no longer raises throughput, using the two terms that grow with B.
answer: past B<sub>crit</sub> the MLP term is math, 2·B·N/C, which grows with B
the KV term B·S<sub>KV</sub>/W also grows with B
the step is proportional to B, so B / T<sub>step</sub> is constant

retrieve.q: Work the book's Pop Quiz at B = 256: 30B dense, int8 weights, bf16 math, v5e 4x4, 8,192 context, 100 kB of KV per token. Give each term and the total.
answer: total ≈ 20.9 ms (book: roughly 21 ms); B = 256 > B<sub>crit</sub> = 120 for int8 weights

retrieve.q: At 8k context and full batch on one H100, a team can either quantize weights to FP8 or halve the KV cache. Which buys more throughput, and why does the formula say so before anyone benchmarks?
answer: the step is 18.91 ms KV + 4.79 ms weights = 23.70 ms, so KV is 80%
FP8 weights only shrink the 4.79 ms term
halving KV bytes both shortens the dominant term and doubles how many sequences fit, so it roughly doubles throughput

compare.q: The critical-batch card studies one matrix; this card studies a whole step. What does adding the KV term change about the conclusion batch up to Bcrit?
answer: for one matrix, throughput rises almost free up to B<sub>crit</sub>
for the whole step, each extra sequence also adds its KV read, so throughput bends over well before B<sub>crit</sub>
and HBM caps the batch: 59 at 8k on one H100, far below 295

compare.q: The consumer-side card explains tokens/s as bandwidth ÷ model size. Where does that rule agree with this formula, and where is it off by 41×?
answer: it agrees at batch 1 with short context: 3.35e12 / 16.06e9 = 209 vs the formula's 205 tok/s
it ignores KV reads and batching
at B = 128 and 2k context the H100 does 8,505 tok/s total (41× the rule) while each user gets 66, not 209

predict.q: Llama-3.1-8B on one H100 at 8k context, B = 16 (step 9.92 ms). Commit first: if you switch to FP8 weights only, by roughly what percentage does the step shrink? And if you instead switch to FP8 KV only?
predict.answer: FP8 weights: the weight read drops from 4.79 to 2.40 ms, so the step goes 9.92 → 7.53 ms, about 24% faster. FP8 KV: the KV read drops from 5.13 to 2.56 ms, so the step goes to 7.36 ms, about 26% faster. At B = 16 the two terms are nearly equal, so the levers are about equal too; at B = 59 (KV 18.9 ms) FP8 KV would win clearly.

apply.task: Extend labs/step-time.py with a row for Llama-3.1-8B on one H100 at 8k context and B = 16. Compute the three terms, the step, per-user and total tokens/s. Then add three variants: FP8 weights (8.03 GB, fp8 math at 1.979e15), FP8 KV (half the KV bytes), and both. Say which term dominates in each.
apply.done: Base: KV 5.13 ms, math 0.26 ms, weights 4.79 ms → 9.92 ms, ≈ 1,613 tok/s. FP8 weights → ≈ 7.53 ms (≈ 2,126 tok/s); FP8 KV → ≈ 7.36 ms; both → ≈ 4.96 ms (≈ 3,225 tok/s), and you've named the dominant term in each.
apply.hint: KV read = 16 × 8,192 × 131,072 B ÷ 3.35e12. Both-FP8: 2.56 ms KV + max(0.13 ms math, 2.40 ms weights).

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong: the FP8-weights saving or the FP8-KV saving?
